children.why_this_cut: Front matter, overview, red-line principles, general principles, risk taxonomy, levels of authority, and definitions. The only crossing linkage is the authority-levels concept (root/system/developer/user/guideline ordering), which is established here and used throughout the chain-of-command section; seeded below.

The chain of command and all subsequent behavioral sections. This child relies on the authority-level ordering and the definitions (assistant, conversation, message roles) established in the first child; no other cross-cutting concepts cross this boundary.

seed_vocabulary.name: authority_level_ordering
seed_vocabulary.prose: The ranking of instruction authority levels: root > system > developer > user > guideline > no authority, used to determine which instruction prevails in conflicts.

seed_vocabulary.name: assistant_definition
seed_vocabulary.prose: The assistant is the entity the end user or developer interacts with; 'model' and 'assistant' are approximately synonymous in this document.

seed_vocabulary.name: conversation_definition
seed_vocabulary.prose: A conversation is a list of messages, each containing a role and content; roles determine authority of instructions.

seed_vocabulary.name: message_role_definition
seed_vocabulary.prose: The role of a message (system, developer, user, assistant, tool) specifies its source and determines authority in conflicts.

seed_vocabulary.name: chain_of_command_principle
seed_vocabulary.prose: The principle that instructions with higher authority override those with lower authority, designed to maximize steerability and control.

expected_cross_links.name: authority_level_ordering
expected_cross_links.evidence: Child 2's chain-of-command section (L183-191) lists the ordering of authority levels and relies on the ranking established at L69-101.

expected_cross_links.name: assistant_definition
expected_cross_links.evidence: Child 2 repeatedly refers to 'the assistant' as the behaving entity; the definition is established at L114-116.

expected_cross_links.name: conversation_definition
expected_cross_links.evidence: Child 2's chain-of-command section refers to 'input conversation' and 'messages' (L181, L193); the conversation/message structure is defined at L118-126.

expected_cross_links.name: message_role_definition
expected_cross_links.evidence: Child 2's chain-of-command section assigns authority to message roles (L183, L193); the role definitions are at L120-125.

expected_cross_links.name: chain_of_command_principle
expected_cross_links.evidence: Child 2's entire chain-of-command section (L171+) operationalizes the principle introduced at L67.

judgment_calls: Chose a 2-child split at L170 (end of Definitions) rather than a 3-child split; the chain-of-command section (L171-800) is cohesive and its internal structure (follow-all-applicable, letter-and-spirit, no-other-objectives, scope, side-effects, assume-best-intentions, ignore-untrusted) is best handled by one child that can divide further. A cut at L110 (after levels of authority) would have split the definitions from the chain of command, requiring more seeds for the definitional concepts.

Seeded five concepts (authority_level_ordering, assistant_definition, conversation_definition, message_role_definition, chain_of_command_principle) because all are established in child 1 and used in child 2. Considered seeding 'applicable_instruction' but it is established within child 2 (L181, L193) and does not cross the cut.
